entities.title: Everyday fixtures
entities.summary: Every fixture in conformance/operations/everyday.json gives its expected status, candidates and diagnostic codes through the JSON layer.
criteria: Each fixture runs as one dynamic test named by its id, through the operation it names (parseIso … toOffset).
The status, the result's operation name and the candidates (compared as JSON) match.
Every code in expect.diagnostics appears among the result's diagnostics.
Rule bundles named by the file are read from the repository, never copied.
entities.details: Run from implementations/java; the test reads the shared files at ../../conformance in place.

entities.title: Text-form fixtures
entities.summary: Every fixture in conformance/operations/text-form.json parses and formats as expected through TextForm.
criteria: Fixtures with direction both or parse: parseText gives the expected status, value and codes.
Fixtures with direction both or format: formatText gives the expected status, text and codes.
entities.details: Run from implementations/java; the test reads the shared files at ../../conformance in place.

entities.title: Structural and Gregorian validation
entities.summary: The structural examples are accepted or rejected, versions and duplicate keys fail closed, and Gregorian validation knows its calendar.
criteria: Every value in conformance/examples/valid.json is valid, and none is invalid as a Gregorian date.
Every value in conformance/examples/invalid-structural.json is rejected with at least one diagnostic.
Other well-formed versions are unsupported; malformed identifiers, unknown properties, unknown kinds and duplicate keys are invalid.
A repeated key is reported as duplicate-key at its JSON pointer; text that is not JSON as utv.json.malformed.
Leap years follow the Gregorian rules for any year; missing days and months are invalid; other calendars are unsupported.
entities.details: Run from implementations/java; the test reads the shared files at ../../conformance in place.

entities.title: Typed layer
entities.summary: At least one test per row of library-api §2, the outcome helpers, text and JSON round trips, constructors, interop on the types and explicit rules.
criteria: Every total operation of §2 returns its plain value, and every partial one its outcome with the expected diagnostic code (month-end, gap, ambiguous, unknown-zone, outside-rule-window, offset-mismatch, needs-leap-seconds, kind-mismatch, reversed-interval).
Outcome helpers never pick silently: single throws OutcomeException, tryGetUnique is empty and uniqueOr gives the fallback unless Unique.
toString round-trips through parse, and fromJson(toJson(v)) equals v.
Constructors reject values that cannot exist; fromJson refuses wrong kinds and values it cannot hold.
ZonedIntent is not Comparable; the context orders zoned values.
The typed java.time adapters convert exactly or report out-of-native-range and precision-loss.
Rules are loaded explicitly, and a context needs them.
entities.details: Run from implementations/java; the test reads the shared files at ../../conformance in place. TypedApiTest.civilTime also pins that 09:30 and 09:30:00 compare as equal; see the source folder's backlog, civil-time-order-ties.

entities.title: One ambiguous diagnostic from compare
entities.summary: TemporalContext.compare reports a single ambiguous warning however many sides fall in an overlap.
criteria: Two wall times in the same New York overlap: multiple, with exactly one diagnostic, ambiguous.
One wall time in an overlap against an instant between its two readings: multiple, with exactly one ambiguous.
entities.details: Uses the demo zone rules through Fixtures.demoZoneRules (examples/).

entities.title: java.time adapters (JSON layer)
entities.summary: The caller names the intent, local-zone readings are refused, lossy conversions say so, and conversions that cannot hold the value are refused.
criteria: LocalDate, LocalTime and LocalDateTime convert both ways; a LocalDateTime becomes a floating date-time, which resolves as symbolic.
An OffsetDateTime becomes an instant, an offset date-time or a local date-time only as asked; +00:00 stays an offset of zero.
A ZonedDateTime keeps its zone and asserts its offset, round-trips, and a ZoneOffset zone becomes a fixed offset.
java.util.Date is accepted only as an instant; civil readings are unsupported.
Converting a zoned value to OffsetDateTime reports zone-dropped; a sub-nanosecond fraction is truncated and reported.
Years beyond LocalDate, missing asserted offsets, time components in a Period and second 60 are refused; a wrong asserted offset is invalid.
entities.details: zonedDateTimeBecomesAZonedIntentionWithItsOffsetAsserted and conversionsThatCannotHoldTheValueAreRefused read the JDK's tz database through ZonedDateTime.
